trickyParts: A paragraph, heading, item or quote line whose whole content is inline raw HTML renders to a line that reads back as an HTML block, which Proof does not accept. The corpus rows keep their mark contexts and gain text around the leaf (`a **<b>** b`, `p **<!a>** q`); without that, TestRenderParseRoundTrip fails on the fixture rather than on the change.

Go's inline declaration rule had to be matched by its block rule. goldmark opens an HTML block at `<![A-Z]` only, so with the inline half alone a lone `<!a>` line was stored by Go as a paragraph the engine reads as an HTML block: 149 documents of the differential's corpora. declarationBlockParser closes that, and such a document is now refused as a lone `<b>` already was.

withoutLeafMarks is composed beside withBlockIds, never folded into it: withBlockIds returns its input unchanged when no id was missing (src/tests/block-ids.test.ts asserts that identity), so a stripped tree folded in would be discarded.

Nothing on the engine's new path goes through Node.fromJSON or doc.check(): the commonmark preset's image parser passes mdast's `title` through as null where its own schema declares a string, so validating there throws for thousands of ordinary documents and a display surface draws the body as its literal source.

C3 needed both readers to move: Go stacked the label's link under the autolink's (no ProseMirror tree holds two marks of one type), and the engine lost the label's link after the inner autolink because @milkdown/transformer closes a mark by type. The hoisted spelling `[a ](u)<https://u.test>[ b](u)` is what Go's renderer already writes and what both readers already read as the target tree.
deviations: The plan's v2 reading for C3 (the label's link not resuming after the inner autolink, copying the engine) was refused by the INFRA-138 architect on 2026-10-29: both readers now keep the label's link on the runs around the autolink. Implemented as the architect decided and as plan v3 records.

The plan's D8 expected 155 divergences against the fork-point engine over the four older corpora; measured here, with this branch's own corpora and the differential's own comparison, 195 over those four (6 in-repo, 125 delimiter, 64 URL) plus 960 over the new leaf-marks corpus. The classes are the plan's; the counts are this run's, over a leaf-marks corpus of 1,753 documents that did not exist when the plan was written.

The census used an exact candidate filter (`<![A-Za-z]` for the declaration and an autolink's own shape inside a bracket run for the label) rather than the plan's wider `\[[^]]*<`. The wide filter's 8,093 candidates are being read as a backstop and its result goes on the pull request; the narrow filter is exact for the two constructs this change touches.
discoveredComplexity: A document whose block is raw HTML alone (a line holding only `<b>`, or `<!a>` after this change) is refused by Go (`block HTML is not accepted by Proof`) and makes the headless engine throw `Cannot create node for doc`, so a comment holding one is drawn as literal text: 28 of the differential's 39,889 documents. Reported to the INFRA-138 architect; it is the shape the planner sent to dispatch://INFRA-722's spec, and this change only makes Go's refusal of a lone `<!a>` match the engine.
